messages.author: 275b133a3506805a
messages.subject: Integrating out censored (truncated) parameters
parts:
Hi all,

So I'm working on this model I have with censored-lognormal hidden
parameters. Now, I don't actually care about those hidden parameters
so I can integrate them out, replacing expressions such as

gap_self ~ lognormal(gap_self_mean, gap_self_stdv) T[timepos[n] -
prevtimes[k],];

with

increment_log_prob(lognormal_ccdf_log(timepos[n] - prevtimes[k],
gap_self_mean, gap_self_stdv));

and thus avoiding having to sample the parameters that create "gap_self".

The full models are here:
* Explicit sampling: <http://tinyurl.com/k2pfcmq>
* Integrating out: <http://tinyurl.com/kfodkff>
* And the toy data: <http://tinyurl.com/kohe2xd> for which the true
parameters are gap_self_mean = 1.23, gap_self_stdv = 0.654.

These models look equivalent to me, but the explicit version
repeatedly gets a good estimate of my test data true parameters, while
the integrating-out version is worse. It should be better, surely,
since it samples a much smaller parameter space. Both approaches get
good Rhat and Neff.

Is there something I've missed in my conversion? Is there any reason
to expect explicit sampling to work better?

Thanks
Dan

messages.author: 3f22b207863d2049
messages.subject: Integrating out censored (truncated) parameters
parts:
Hi Dan,
You might be interested in some of the later messages in the following thread: https://groups.google.com/forum/m/#!searchin/stan-users/Luc/stan-users/65nVen9sIsM

To my understanding, the cause may be that cdf and pdf functions have different levels of numerical stability (pdf>>cdf), such that mixing is sometimes better when using the pdf to estimate a censored observation.

Luc

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Integrating out censored (truncated) parameters
parts:
Hi,

Thanks for the clue! That clue led me to try a version which keeps the
explicit sampling, but uses increment_log_prob():
<http://tinyurl.com/lkk5ady>. It works, converges as nicely as the
original. (More specifically the true vals are always within the
5%-95%iles, as in the original, and unlike the integrated-out
version.) So... well, that's interesting. I wonder if it's specific to
stan's methods, or a more general thing to know.

I needed to convert to increment_log_prob() because I want to add a
mixture-model aspect. So this might be the way.

Thanks
Dan
